verdict: Avoid new garment and made-ups exposure in Tiruppur for now; only lend to organised, domestic-order, low-leverage units with tight monthly structure, and decline migrant-labour-dependent job-work units.
title: Tiruppur Readymade Garments & Made-ups: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
Tiruppur converts yarn and fabric into knitted garments and made-up sets, mostly for export buyers, and gets paid after the buyer ships and accepts. **Cash sits in fabric and finished-goods inventory and in export receivables, not in the machines.** The unit's margin is thin and set by the buyer, so pricing power is weak; the cost base is raw material plus labour, and bonus is a real annual cash call. Bonus disbursement for textile and apparel workers here is underway and expected to finish across most units by November 5 [1]. So when a proposal lands, check the bonus and wage payout calendar against the drawing power; if the unit has no headroom for the November payout, ask how it is funded.

## What has changed now
**The national demand signal is negative and Tamil Nadu is weaker than India.** IIP for NIC 14 output is -7.4% YoY [D], output is -5.6% Apr-to-date [D], and exports are -6.2% Apr-to-date in USD [D]. Tamil Nadu GST collections are -3.2% Apr-to-date against India +6.1% [D]. Local reporting says industry leaders flag a noticeable slowdown in incoming orders [1]. **Treat this as a demand-side break, not a seasonal dip.** The Christmas family-set line is drawing foreign buyers [2][3], but that is one product story, not a recovery.

## Where the growth is
**Pursue organised units with confirmed domestic and European order books and in-house processing.** Peer Raymond Lifestyle shows garmenting driving growth with an order book through mid-Feb'27 and rising European traction, though cost pressure dented 2Q [4]. Sangam shows revenue growth projected but net profit collapsing to Rs.4.3 Cr in Q4 FY26 from Rs.12.8 Cr [5]. So when a proposal lands, check the order book date and buyer concentration; if the book ends before the loan tenor, ask for the buyer-wise confirmed order list. **Avoid migrant-labour-dependent job-work units and pure export converters** — bonus opacity in non-unionised units is flagged locally [1], and export-linked sectors see moderation [10].

## How to grow safely
**Structure short: 12-month working capital, monthly drawing power against stock and receivables, no term loan for capacity.** Take stock statement, debtor ageing and GST returns every month, plus the bonus payout proof in November. **Covenant on receivables days and inventory turns, tested monthly.** Rating methodology ties working capital intensity to inventory and receivables [8], and leverage-heavy units are more vulnerable in downturns [11]. If receivables days stretch beyond the stated cycle, ask for buyer confirmation before enhancing limits.

## Early-warning signs
- **Order book shortening or buyer concentration rising** — check monthly; if the top buyer crosses half of sales, cut limit.
- **GST turnover falling below the prior quarter** — check monthly; if two consecutive falls, freeze enhancement.
- **Bonus or wage payment delayed past November 5** [1] — check in November; if delayed, ask for funding source and reassess.
- **Inventory build with flat sales** — check monthly; if stock rises while billing falls, reduce drawing power.
